label: Snowflake
description: Tools to query and explore Snowflake with per-user, per-role access

tools.name: WhoAmI
tools.description: Return the authenticated Snowflake identity and session defaults. Call this FIRST. Grounds who the session acts as (user + current role) and the default warehouse/database/schema a query uses when you do not override them.

output.description: The Snowflake user, role, account, warehouse, database, and schema in effect.

tools.name: ListDatabases
tools.description: List the databases your role can access. Snowflake returns only databases your current role is granted, so this is already a per-user answer.

output.description: A list of database names the caller's role can access.

tools.name: ListSchemas
tools.description: List the schemas in a database that your role can access. Call ListDatabases first for a valid database.

output.description: A list of schemas (database, name) the caller's role can access.

tools.name: ListTables
tools.description: List the tables and views in a schema that your role can query. Each row includes `fqn`, a ready-to-use quoted fully-qualified name you drop straight into Query.

parameters.name: include_views
parameters.description: Include views as well as tables. Default is true.

output.description: A list of objects (database, schema_name, name, kind, fqn) the role can query.

tools.name: DescribeTable
tools.description: List a table or view's columns (name, type, nullable, default, comment). Use before writing a query so you can select exact columns instead of SELECT *.

output.description: A list of columns with name, type, nullability, default, and comment.

tools.name: Query
tools.description: Run a SQL query and return the rows, plus the identity Snowflake ran them under. The query executes under your authenticated Snowflake identity, so your role and Snowflake's row/masking policies decide what you can read. Reference tables with the `fqn` from ListTables, or use bare names with database/schema_name.

parameters.name: sql
parameters.description: The SQL to run. Reference tables with the fqn from ListTables, or bare names plus database/schema_name.

parameters.name: database
parameters.description: Session database so bare table names resolve. Omit to use your default.

parameters.name: schema_name
parameters.description: Session schema so bare table names resolve. Omit to use your default.

parameters.name: warehouse
parameters.description: Warehouse to run on. Omit if WhoAmI shows a default warehouse.

parameters.name: max_rows
parameters.description: Maximum rows to return. Default is 100, hard cap 1000.

parameters.name: timeout_seconds
parameters.description: Abort the query if it runs longer than this many seconds. Default is 120, up to 3600.

output.description: The rows, the columns, the row_count, a truncated flag, and the user/role Snowflake enforced them under.

summary:
## Arcade Snowflake Toolkit

Query Snowflake from your agents with **per-user, per-role access**. Every end user authenticates as themselves via OAuth, and each query runs under that user's own Snowflake identity, so Snowflake's RBAC, row-access, and masking policies decide what each user sees. Two users running the same query get different data. The toolkit holds **no shared credential** and enforces **no policy of its own**. Snowflake is the boundary.

## How it works

1. A user connects the Snowflake provider once (OAuth). Arcade brokers and silently refreshes a short-lived, per-user access token.
2. Every tool call opens a connection with `authenticator=oauth` under that user's token, so `CURRENT_USER()` and `CURRENT_ROLE()` are the real person and all governance applies to them.
3. Agents discover what a user can reach with the `List*`/`DescribeTable` tools (which run Snowflake's own access-filtered `SHOW`/`DESCRIBE`), then run a query.

## Configure on the Arcade side

1. In the Arcade dashboard, add a **Custom OAuth 2.0 provider** with id `snowflake`:
   - **Authorization URL:** `https://<account>.snowflakecomputing.com/oauth/authorize`
   - **Token URL:** `https://<account>.snowflakecomputing.com/oauth/token-request`
   - **Client ID / Secret:** from your Snowflake OAuth security integration (below).
   - **Scopes:** `refresh_token` (lets Arcade refresh the short-lived access token).
2. Copy the **Redirect URL** Arcade generates. You register it in Snowflake next.
3. Set the toolkit secret **`SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT`** to your account identifier in connector form, e.g. `AB12345.us-east-1` (the org-account form `MYORG-MYACCOUNT` also works). This is just the address of your account, not a credential.

## Configure on the Snowflake side

Run as `ACCOUNTADMIN`:

```sql
-- 1) OAuth security integration; register Arcade's redirect URL
CREATE SECURITY INTEGRATION arcade_oauth
  TYPE = OAUTH
  OAUTH_CLIENT = CUSTOM
  OAUTH_CLIENT_TYPE = 'CONFIDENTIAL'
  OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI = '<redirect-url-from-arcade>'
  OAUTH_ISSUE_REFRESH_TOKENS = TRUE
  OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN_VALIDITY = 86400
  ENABLED = TRUE;

-- Read the client id + secret to paste into the Arcade provider (arg UPPERCASE)
SELECT SYSTEM$SHOW_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRETS('ARCADE_OAUTH');
```

Then give each end user a **read-only role** scoped to exactly the data they may see, and set it as their `DEFAULT_ROLE` (recipes below). The role is the access boundary.

## Read-only and access restrictions

By default, this integration manages access entirely through **Snowflake roles**. Whatever role a user has is what Arcade enforces for them, so a user bound to a read-only role is read-only. For extra, per-agent restrictions on top, add an Arcade **Contextual Access** prehook policy that can, for example, restrict an agent to read-only queries.

## Admin guidance: Snowflake roles

Give the right role to the right user. Common recipes:

```sql
-- Create a read-only role scoped to a slice of data
CREATE ROLE IF NOT EXISTS ANALYST_READ;
GRANT USAGE  ON DATABASE  MY_DB                      TO ROLE ANALYST_READ;
GRANT USAGE  ON SCHEMA    MY_DB.MY_SCHEMA            TO ROLE ANALYST_READ;
GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA MY_DB.MY_SCHEMA TO ROLE ANALYST_READ;
GRANT USAGE  ON WAREHOUSE MY_WH                      TO ROLE ANALYST_READ;

-- Finer than a table: expose a view (grant the view, NOT the base table) to
-- limit columns, or use masking / row-access policies (Enterprise edition) to
-- limit cells and rows per user.

-- Assign the role to a user and make it their default
GRANT ROLE ANALYST_READ TO USER SOME_USER;
ALTER USER SOME_USER SET DEFAULT_ROLE = ANALYST_READ DEFAULT_WAREHOUSE = MY_WH;

-- Inspect / analyze roles
SHOW GRANTS TO ROLE ANALYST_READ;   -- privileges and roles this role holds
SHOW GRANTS TO USER SOME_USER;       -- roles granted to a user
SHOW GRANTS OF ROLE ANALYST_READ;    -- who holds this role
DESC USER SOME_USER;                 -- default role / warehouse / namespace
```

## Caveats

- Each end user must resolve to a distinct Snowflake identity with an appropriate role; the toolkit differentiates by **identity**, not by query text.
- The connection **role** determines read-only-ness. A user bound to a write-capable role can write; bind read-only roles for a read-only deployment.
- `SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT` must use the connector form `<locator>.<region>` (or the org-account form). Do not hand-build `<org>-<locator>`.
- Cell/row governance (masking and row-access policies) requires Snowflake **Enterprise edition** and above.
